Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

please turn this into a useful prompt for a desk guide, not the guide itself. it’s a fictional Northline Rail ticket exchange at the Larkspur station desk, and the details below are the information the writer should work from. Samira Cole came to the desk on May 9 about one ticket for travel from Larkspur to Bellford on May 14. Her booking reference is NL-48271. It is one adult passenger, travelling on the direct Northline service, with no transfer. The ticket is for the 09:20 train; it cost $48, and her seat is 18C. She has the ticket in the app and also brought a printed copy, so the guide can say either format is acceptable for looking up the booking, but it shouldn’t imply that both are required. The desk can use the booking reference if she has it, and the passenger name is Samira Cole. She says, “My appointment moved, and I can leave later, but I need to arrive before 2:30.” The original train reaches Bellford at 11:50, so that still meets the time she gave, but she’s asking about changing to the later 11:05 service. The 11:05 reaches Bellford at 13:35. It is the one she has in mind, not a different route or destination.

The guide should explain the exchange rules in plain language without turning them into a promise that a seat or fare will remain available. This ticket can be exchanged once, only for the same passenger and the same Larkspur-to-Bellford route, and only before the original 09:20 train departs. The exchange fee is $8. If the new fare is higher, the passenger pays the difference as well as the fee. If the new fare is lower, there is no fare-difference refund and no travel credit; the $8 fee still applies. The ticket cannot be exchanged after the original train has departed. A replacement seat is assigned when an exchange is completed, so don’t carry seat 18C over to a new train or promise that Samira will have a particular seat. The desk must check the live seat inventory and fare at the time it handles the request; the figures that follow are a May 9 snapshot, not a guarantee for May 14.

At that snapshot, the 11:05 has seats available and its fare is $56. The fare is $8 more than the original $48, so if that train is still available when the agent checks and Samira confirms the change, the amount collected is $16 total: an $8 fare difference plus the $8 exchange fee. The agent should say what makes up the total rather than just saying “sixteen dollars.” Don’t say the exchange has happened just because the passenger asked about it. It is completed only after availability has been checked, Samira has confirmed that she wants the change, and the full amount due has been paid. If any of those steps is missing, her current booking remains the 09:20 service and seat 18C; don’t describe the new train or a new seat as booked.

There’s also a 13:40 direct service in the May 9 snapshot, with seats available at a fare of $42. It reaches Bellford at 16:10, which is after the time Samira said she needs to arrive. The guide may mention it only as a possible later option if she says that arriving after 2:30 is acceptable; it must not present the 13:40 as meeting her stated arrival need. Its lower fare does not create a refund or credit under the stated rules, and the $8 fee still applies if she chooses it. The snapshot does not establish what inventory or fare will be when the desk processes the exchange, so have the agent check rather than treating the listed availability as current.

Please organize the eventual prompt so it asks for an internal desk guide with practical wording the agent can use with Samira, plus a short sequence of checks. Keep the guide grounded in this single fictional case, but make it usable at the desk: it should cover identifying the booking from the reference or passenger name, confirming the route and travel date, checking the live train and fare, explaining the applicable fee and difference, and confirming before processing. Keep the wording calm and ordinary. It should distinguish the May 9 snapshot from a live check, and distinguish an offer from a completed exchange. The guide should not suggest that the passenger must show both the app and printed ticket, should not move her to another route, and should not promise a replacement seat. It should avoid legalistic language and avoid adding policies that are not in these notes.

1. If the requested 11:05 train still has a seat available when the agent checks, and Samira confirms the change and pays the $16 total, instruct the guide to describe completing the one permitted exchange for the same route and passenger. State that a replacement seat is assigned as part of completion, without specifying its number. If the 11:05 is no longer available, do not complete that requested change; tell Samira it is unavailable and offer the 13:40 only after making clear that it arrives at 16:10, or leave her on the original 09:20 booking if she needs to arrive before 2:30. If she does not confirm or does not pay the amount due, also leave the original booking unchanged. Keep those outcomes conditional, rather than choosing one in advance. The guide should make clear that the 13:40 alternative is relevant only if she relaxes her arrival-time requirement and it is available when checked; it does not solve the stated before-2:30 need.

Please make the final section useful rather than ending with a generic customer-service reminder: it should tell the agent how to close the conversation without implying a change was made when it was not. For an exchange that is actually completed, the wording should confirm the new train and that a new seat has been assigned, without inventing its number. If no exchange is completed, it should confirm that the original 09:20 train and seat 18C remain in place, and that no fare or booking change has been made. Do not assume the agent has already checked the live inventory, collected payment, received confirmation, or completed either branch.", "output": "Create an internal desk guide for a fictional Northline Rail ticket exchange at the Larkspur station desk. Keep the guide grounded in this case, use calm, ordinary language, and do not add policies or details that are not provided.

### Case details
Samira Cole came to the desk on May 9 about booking NL-48271, for one adult passenger travelling direct from Larkspur to Bellford on May 14. Her original train is the 09:20 service, which arrives at 11:50. The $48 ticket assigns seat 18C. Samira has the ticket in the app and a printed copy; either format is acceptable for looking up the booking, and she does not need to show both. The agent can use booking reference NL-48271 or her name.

Samira says, “My appointment moved, and I can leave later, but I need to arrive before 2:30.” She is asking about the later 11:05 direct service, which arrives at 13:35. Do not change the route or destination.

### Exchange rules and May 9 snapshot
The ticket may be exchanged once, only for the same passenger and the same Larkspur-to-Bellford route, and only before the original 09:20 train departs. The exchange fee is $8. If the new fare is higher, the passenger pays the fare difference as well as the fee. If the new fare is lower, there is no fare-difference refund or travel credit, and the $8 fee still applies. The ticket cannot be exchanged after the original train has departed. A replacement seat is assigned when an exchange is completed; do not carry over seat 18C or promise a particular new seat.

The following availability and fares are a May 9 snapshot only, not a guarantee for May 14 or for the time the request is processed. The agent must check live inventory and fare before proceeding:
- The 11:05 direct train has seats available in the snapshot and costs $56. That is $8 more than the original fare, making the total due $16: an $8 fare difference plus the $8 exchange fee. Explain the two parts of the total rather than simply saying “sixteen dollars.”
- The 13:40 direct train has seats available in the snapshot and costs $42. It arrives at 16:10, after Samira’s stated arrival deadline. Mention it only if she says arriving after 2:30 is acceptable. Its lower fare does not produce a refund or credit, and the $8 fee still applies if she chooses it.

### Checks and conditional action
Ask the guide to direct the agent to identify the booking using the reference or passenger name, confirm the passenger, route, and travel date, and check the live availability and fare for the requested train. Explain the applicable fee and fare difference, then obtain Samira’s confirmation and payment before completing an exchange. An inquiry or offer alone does not change the booking. If availability has not been checked, Samira has not confirmed, or the amount due has not been paid, do not describe an exchange as completed.

1. **If the 11:05 is still available when checked:** If Samira confirms the change and pays the $16 total, complete the one permitted exchange for the same passenger and route. Confirm the new train and say that a replacement seat has been assigned, without giving a seat number.
2. **If the 11:05 is no longer available:** Do not complete the requested change. Tell Samira it is unavailable. Offer the 13:40 only if it is available when checked and she says the 16:10 arrival is acceptable; make clear that it does not meet her stated before-2:30 requirement. Otherwise, leave her on the original 09:20 booking if she needs to arrive before 2:30. If she does not confirm a change or does not pay the amount due, leave the original booking unchanged.

Close the conversation according to what actually happened. If an exchange was completed, confirm the new train and that a new seat has been assigned, without inventing its number. If no exchange was completed, confirm that the original 09:20 train and seat 18C remain in place and that no fare or booking change was made. Do not assume that live inventory was checked, payment was collected, Samira confirmed, or either branch was completed."}]
